title: Agere: how every layer contributes to an answer
scope: Named components from the handoff, current code/model registry, original atlas, all registered PRODUCT analytic engines, and named research/candidate branches. A component is a model, mechanism or product subsystem, not every Python function or dependency.

components.name: Native feed parsers
components.job: Read X12 837/835/834, NCPDP, HL7 v2, FHIR bulk, CMS CCLF/ALR and Epic/athena/eCW extracts.
components.why: Claims, payments, enrollment and clinical events have different structures and revision rules; preserve their meaning before querying.
components.economics: Parse and normalize once; reuse the resulting records.
components.status: Implemented; adapter coverage is format-specific.

components.name: Warehouse connectors and workspaces
components.job: Connect to Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Postgres, SQLite, DuckDB and file drops through configured adapters.
components.why: Bind queries to the customer’s actual schema and snapshot rather than a generic invented database.
components.economics: Workspace profiling and mapping are reused across questions.
components.status: Implemented; each connection requires its SDK/configuration.

components.name: Profiling, mapping and activation
components.job: Profile fields and values, map canonical domains, retain raw tables, persist mapping review and run workspace verification.
components.why: A correct-looking query is useless if a source field was mapped to the wrong concept. Raw passthrough retains access beyond modeled tables.
components.economics: Resolve recurring mappings once; avoid rediscovering schema on each question.
components.status: Implemented; ambiguous mappings retain review states.

components.name: Identity, revisions and source clocks
components.job: Keep patient identity, record versions, event dates and arrival dates.
components.why: Avoid mixing people, counting replacements twice, or using evidence that arrived after the requested cutoff.
components.economics: Shared preprocessing replaces repeated chart reconstruction.
components.status: Core data contracts.

components.name: Canonical records and semantic SQL layer
components.job: Expose patient, encounter, measurement, medication, enrollment, claim and payment meanings as queryable entities.
components.why: Keep order, fill, use and administration distinct; preserve reversals and the meaning of financial amounts.
components.economics: Reusable SQL tables make common answers computational rather than generative.
components.status: Core; source support varies by workspace.

components.name: Codes, aliases and domain definitions
components.job: Use explicit ICD/SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm/NDC and other received code mappings and controlled vocabularies.
components.why: Connect user language to the appropriate condition, measurement or medication without relying on name similarity alone.
components.economics: Deterministic mappings avoid hosted interpretation for known terms.
components.status: Exact code/alias matching precedes embedding fallback.

components.name: Patient state and source-bound assertions
components.job: Track assertion, subject, time, relation, conflicts and missing evidence separately.
components.why: A past family-history mention must not become a current patient condition; a planned referral must not become completed care.
components.economics: Structured assertions can be reused by multiple queries.
components.status: Implemented bounded interpretation; unresolved facts remain unresolved.

components.name: PDFKit and Apple Vision OCR
components.job: Extract text from PDFs and scans with source coordinates.
components.why: Make non-tabular source material inspectable and retain its relationship to the original document.
components.economics: Native extraction avoids a hosted model call for routine OCR.
components.status: Native extraction path; OCR quality still matters.

components.name: BM25 lexical retrieval
components.job: Rank candidate passages or schema items by exact words and weighted term matches.
components.why: Medical codes, drug names and rare field names can matter more than broad semantic similarity.
components.economics: Cheap local candidate selection.
components.status: Used in lexical/hybrid retrieval.

components.name: Reciprocal-rank fusion
components.job: Merge lexical and dense rankings without treating their raw scores as interchangeable.
components.why: A candidate found by one retrieval method can survive even when the other misses it.
components.economics: Combines existing search signals without another generative call.
components.status: Used in passage/catalog retrieval.

components.name: BGE reranker v2-m3
components.job: Score a question and each shortlisted passage together, then reorder candidates.
components.why: Separate passages that merely mention the topic from those more directly relevant to the question.
components.economics: Spend local reranking compute on a shortlist; send less irrelevant text to downstream models.
components.status: Available on indexed retrieval paths; not every workspace has a passage index.
components.example: Question: did the patient decline treatment? A directly relevant refusal passage should outrank a general drug mention.

components.name: Learned schema reranker
components.job: Rank tables, columns, streams, fields and stored values using lexical, embedding and small logistic-model features.
components.why: A SQL writer needs the right field and exact stored value; hiding them in a huge catalog creates avoidable query errors.
components.economics: A focused schema slice uses fewer prompt tokens.
components.status: Integrated schema-selection layer.

components.name: Source windows and protected evidence
components.job: Keep full token windows, source offsets, patient/date scope and protected exception passages.
components.why: Avoid silent truncation or dropping the sentence that changes the interpretation. Top-ranked snippets still do not establish complete population coverage.
components.economics: Bound the material being interpreted while preserving traceability.
components.status: Index-dependent; missing indexes are explicit.

components.name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
components.job: Compact local embeddings for candidate-plan matching, routing features and eligible query reuse.
components.why: Recognize related phrasing without making a large model regenerate a known analysis.
components.economics: Local embeddings and cached vectors avoid repeated hosted routing.
components.status: Installed; role depends on route and workspace.

components.name: Granite Embedding English R2
components.job: Create dense representations of source passages for semantic retrieval.
components.why: Find relevant wording even when the question and note use different terms.
components.economics: Local indexed retrieval narrows downstream context.
components.status: Installed retrieval branch; not an extra mandatory encoder on every query.

components.name: UltraBERT-Embed-150M
components.job: Retrieve raw-catalog streams and propose lab/condition terminology matches when codes and aliases fail.
components.why: Find the relevant source outside the modeled fast path, and connect unfamiliar source labels to known concepts.
components.economics: Cache catalog vectors; encode the new question locally.
components.status: Enabled by default when available; thresholded fallback. Not the MiniLM router or semantic cache.
components.example: It can propose a matching lab concept; below-threshold matches remain proposals. Medication brands use the explicit brand table instead.

components.name: BioClinical-ModernBERT-base
components.job: Encode clinical text into features for task-specific heads and alternative action proposals.
components.why: Clinical representations give a small downstream classifier more context than isolated keywords.
components.economics: Reuse frozen local features; a small head can be cheaper than repeated generative reading.
components.status: Installed; research/training branches. Not a universal accepted clinical reader.

components.name: Jev 1.13.0
components.job: Return constrained evidence decisions and probability distributions under a typed question/choice contract.
components.why: Distinguish affirmed, negated, historical, other-person, hypothetical or unresolved statements rather than accepting any mention as fact.
components.economics: Bounded classification can avoid generating a long explanation for every excerpt; hosted usage is metered.
components.status: Selectable typed reader; optional therapy-barrier cascade begins with Jev.
components.example: “Could not afford the refill” affirms an access barrier. “Mother could not afford it” does not establish this patient’s barrier.

components.name: Perplexity Decisions · pplx-decider-v1.1-27b
components.job: Use the same typed evidence contract as Jev; also choose among complete registered analysis recipes.
components.why: Overlap with Jev enables alternatives, comparison or escalation. Its routing role checks whether a known plan covers the entire question.
components.economics: A bounded decision can avoid an open-ended frontier plan. Calls are hosted and metered.
components.status: Selectable reader; configured plan decider. Neither model’s agreement proves truth.
components.example: Jev and Perplexity are alternative implementations of a decision role; they are not two obligatory stages of every answer.

components.name: Qwen3-4B + narrow LoRA
components.job: Translate unfamiliar phrasing into compact cohort-family slots, then round-trip those slots through the deterministic parser.
components.why: The local model handles language variation while existing code retains responsibility for definitions and SQL.
components.economics: Distill reusable work into local inference; no new hosted tokens on an accepted local path. Training and compute still cost resources.
components.status: Implemented optional slot-filling path; flag default off.
components.example: Question → family/condition/window slots → parser → validated SQL. It does not invent ICD code sets.

components.name: Qwen3-4B + SQL LoRA
components.job: Propose SQL locally from learned question/SQL pairs, with read-only execution and result-agreement checks.
components.why: Attempts to reuse prior successful query patterns on new phrasing, but free-form SQL has more failure modes than narrow slots.
components.economics: Could reduce repeated hosted SQL-writing cost where accepted.
components.status: Implemented experiment; default off after insufficient broad SQL performance. Separate from narrow-slot Qwen.

components.name: Kev 4B
components.job: Use a local trained pointer/decision head under the bounded reader interface.
components.why: Test whether a purpose-built local decision architecture can replace hosted classification for a specific role.
components.economics: Potential local inference economics; no hosted call for local execution.
components.status: Executed research comparison; did not meet promotion criteria.

components.name: Liquid d1-3B
components.job: Use a native local decision readout under the same bounded task contract.
components.why: Provides another local implementation to compare on the same evidence and labels.
components.economics: Potential local decision cost reduction.
components.status: Executed research comparison; did not replace the default reader.

components.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
components.job: Fill bounded metric/operator slots, choose composer tools and produce optional prose.
components.why: Map language to known computation without asking a large model to recreate the underlying mathematics.
components.economics: Smaller hosted calls where bounded interpretation suffices.
components.status: Configured task-specific helper; not the current three-analyst default.

components.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
components.job: Propose policy-search candidates; remain available in configured alternate and historical analyst policies.
components.why: Use a capable proposer for sandboxed policy search while separating candidate generation from evaluation.
components.economics: Task-specific alternative; paid calls only when that route runs.
components.status: Policy-search default proposer; historical baseline/alternate analyst roles.

components.name: Claude Opus 5.5
components.job: Generate analysis contracts/SQL for unclaimed questions and compose tool-grounded deliverables.
components.why: Extend beyond known question templates while keeping executable queries and tool-produced numbers.
components.economics: Reserve frontier inference for coverage and synthesis that need it. Three analysts cost more than one call.
components.status: Current fallback: three analyst proposals plus at most one bounded mechanical repair/tie-break.

components.name: TF-IDF and logistic task heads
components.job: Classify assertion/barrier types, route intents and rank schema or briefing candidates with fitted small models.
components.why: Learn recurring distinctions cheaply; use role-specific features and acceptance thresholds.
components.economics: Local prediction avoids hosted calls on accepted cases.
components.status: Several task-specific heads; calibration and supervision differ by task.

components.name: Intent router
components.job: Distinguish a question, plan, simulation and requested deliverable.
components.why: Choose the right workflow before answering; a request for a report is not just a scalar query.
components.economics: Avoid dispatching the entire stack to the wrong task.
components.status: Product entry routing.

components.name: Deterministic compiler
components.job: Parse recognized question meaning into a typed execution graph.
components.why: Keep requested filters, dates, grouping and answer shape explicit; reject unrepresented qualifiers.
components.economics: Known question forms need no hosted planning.
components.status: Core first-choice path for supported language.

components.name: Cohort, data-quality and VBC SQL families
components.job: Fill reusable parameterized query shapes with the question’s stated definition.
components.why: Preserve the denominator and date logic across many combinations without a custom query for every wording.
components.economics: Code renders SQL; only unresolved language may need model assistance.
components.status: Specialist families with role-specific acceptance gates.

components.name: Governed metric and operator routers
components.job: Select a defined metric or analytical engine and validate its parameters.
components.why: A count, survival curve, forecast and causal-effect question require different calculations.
components.economics: Reuse engine code; local routing is attempted before paid selection where supported.
components.status: Implemented local/hosted routes.

components.name: Exact and semantic query reuse
components.job: Reuse eligible verified plans/queries with matching source/semantic context and identical critical slots.
components.why: A similar sentence with a different payer, threshold or date must not inherit the old answer.
components.economics: Skip repeated interpretation; execute the eligible reused query against its bound context.
components.status: Exact and guarded paraphrase reuse; semantic reuse is of queries, not arbitrary answer text.

components.name: Specialist-first dispatch
components.job: Allow a sufficiently covered specialist route to answer; escalate unclaimed questions.
components.why: Use the method suited to the task while retaining a route for novel questions.
components.economics: Avoid paying frontier analysts for every ordinary query.
components.status: Current policy; preserves missing-input declines.

components.name: Typed graphs and contracts
components.job: Validate allowed operations, parameter types, dependencies and output shape.
components.why: Prevent malformed plans and mismatched output types from silently becoming answers.
components.economics: Catch mechanical errors before costly downstream work.
components.status: Core shared execution contract.

components.name: Read-only SQL and result checks
components.job: Execute proposed SQL in the system, with lint, bounds and sanity checks.
components.why: A model’s stated number is not a computed result; execution reveals invalid queries and some inconsistencies.
components.economics: Use database computation; bounded repair instead of unlimited retries.
components.status: Integrated; passing checks does not prove semantic correctness.

components.name: Hybrid analyst contract and adjudication
components.job: Compare three analyst proposals/results and use one bounded repair/tie-break when needed.
components.why: Expose disagreements and recover mechanical failures on unfamiliar questions.
components.economics: Higher cost is reserved for unclaimed questions; same-model errors can remain correlated.
components.status: Current Opus fallback policy.

components.name: Raw-catalog and empty-result guard
components.job: Probe received source catalogs when the fast path is insufficient or results need scrutiny.
components.why: A missing modeled table or empty query result should not automatically mean the event never happened.
components.economics: Local catalog selection focuses any necessary SQL/model escalation.
components.status: Integrated answer-guard routes.

components.name: Learn-then-Test and calibration gates
components.job: Bind acceptance thresholds to a calibrated task, model, code and evaluation distribution.
components.why: A fast route should claim only the scope it can support; stale or uncertified gates must be visible.
components.economics: Trade coverage for fewer accepted errors; escalate the remaining cases.
components.status: Conditional certificates, not a universal accuracy guarantee.

components.name: Source-linked evidence review
components.job: Request a bounded Jev/Perplexity reading for an exact patient, source span and assertion.
components.why: Keep the evidence question distinct from diagnosis, treatment approval or complete-chart conclusions.
components.economics: Review the unresolved portion; cache identical validated requests.
components.status: Selectable explicit review routes.

components.name: Explain
components.job: WHY questions: what drives / contributes to / is associated with an outcome (readmission, a condition, a lab threshold).
components.why: Separate measured associations from a fluent but unsupported explanation.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Factor statistics

components.name: Discover
components.job: WHERE / which groups: unexpected concentrations of an outcome across practices, PCPs, payers, age, sex, social needs (hotspots nobody specified).
components.why: Search many subgroups while accounting for the multiple comparisons problem.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Segment discovery and BH false-discovery control

components.name: Trajectory
components.job: Per-patient lab or vital trends: WHICH PATIENTS are declining or will cross a threshold (Kalman forecast), change points. Population-level "what fraction reach X within T" is survival.
components.why: Use the order and noise of repeated measurements instead of comparing two arbitrary values.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Kalman filtering, forecasts and change points

components.name: Survival
components.job: Time-to-event: HOW QUICKLY / HOW LONG UNTIL / median days until / what fraction reach an event within a time: readmission or follow-up after discharge, time from diagnosis to an event or lab threshold (e.g. eGFR < 30 within 2 years); Kaplan-Meier by group, log-rank, Cox hazard ratios. A single observed share (e.g. what share of discharges were followed by another admission within N days) with no curve, censoring or time-until wording is literal_lookup.
components.why: Handle event timing and censoring rather than treating incomplete follow-up as no event.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Kaplan–Meier, log-rank and Cox

components.name: Vbc
components.job: Value-based care: member months, attribution, utilization per 1,000, PMPM cost, risk score, quality measures (measure library: HEDIS/Stars/eCQM approximations such as GSD, CBP, KED, breast and colorectal screening, depression screening, FMC, TRC, PCR, AHRQ PQI 90/91/92, Part D PDC adherence, the MSSP APP Plus set, with care-gap patient lists), shared-savings settlement and its risk (VaR), fair (Shapley) split of savings, cost change decomposition. Settlement under a named program (MSSP BASIC A-E / ENHANCED, ACO REACH, LEAD) uses the cited program rulebook terms. PMPM is reported as observed allowed PMPM; the IBNR-completed figure leads only when completion or IBNR is asked.
components.why: Keep enrollment exposure, observed payments, completion estimates and contract terms distinct.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Member months, PMPM, claims completion, quality and settlement arithmetic

components.name: Program Effect
components.job: Did a program or medication start work: care management, transitions of care, community services, care coordination, starting a drug class; effect on ED visits, admissions, PMPM or a lab.
components.why: Compare outcomes with an explicit counterfactual method instead of calling a before/after change an effect.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Difference-in-differences and synthetic controls

components.name: Outreach
components.job: Who should we call / prioritise: a capacity-limited outreach worklist ranked by expected value with reasons (care gaps, rising risk, social needs, utilization).
components.why: Make a feasible worklist given limited slots; high risk alone does not establish treatment benefit.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Capacity-constrained expected-value selection

components.name: Calibration
components.job: How well calibrated / how accurate are our forecasts and risk scores: time-split conformal backtest coverage, Brier score, ECE, reliability tables.
components.why: Check whether uncertainty and risk scores behave as advertised.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Time-split backtests, conformal coverage, Brier score and ECE

components.name: Monitor
components.job: Is anything out of control: SPC control charts of ED/admit rates, PMPM, lab volume, denial rate, arrival lag; data-feed breaks; claims integrity, Benford, peer outliers, duplicates.
components.why: Separate unusual changes needing investigation from ordinary variation; flags are not proof of fraud or care failure.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: EWMA/CUSUM, control charts, Benford and outlier checks

components.name: Market
components.job: What moved / markets view: each practice, PCP or payer as a ticker for ED and admission rates, PMPM, A1c and BP control, denial and no-show rates; change vs prior month and baseline, trend, volatility, beta to the network, moves ranked by surprise x impact, network-wide vs one-practice moves.
components.why: Distinguish a network-wide movement from a provider-specific change.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Changes, volatility, beta and surprise × impact

components.name: Demand
components.job: Volume forecasts: ED visits, admissions, appointments, discharges or bed-days per week/month with intervals and backtest vs naive; beds needed at a target occupancy and peak day; staffing from user-supplied ratios.
components.why: Estimate future demand with uncertainty rather than extrapolating a single number.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Volume forecasts, intervals and naive-baseline backtests

components.name: Profile
components.job: Fair PCP/practice comparison: which units are truly high or low on ED use, admissions, readmissions, A1c control or PMPM after panel size and case mix (shrunk rates, credibility, rank intervals).
components.why: Avoid penalizing small panels for unstable raw rates.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Empirical Bayes shrinkage, credibility and rank intervals

components.name: Pathway
components.job: Care pathways / patient journeys: where patients go after an ED visit, discharge or PCP visit, follow-up within N days vs ED return, leakage to outside organisations, most common paths, chance of admission within N steps or days. Use for the SEQUENCE of next steps; for how quickly / median days until one event, use survival.
components.why: Reconstruct where patients went next instead of reducing the journey to unrelated counts.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Event-sequence and transition analysis

components.name: Briefing
components.job: What should I look at today / morning briefing / what needs my attention: the proactive briefing of the most important findings across discovery, trajectories, forecasts, cost and utilization changes, outliers, monitor and market moves, ranked by a learning-to-rank model (information x impact prior, feedback-trained) with the reason for each position.
components.why: Prioritize useful findings rather than flooding the user with every statistically unusual result.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Information × impact ranking, feedback learning and exploration

components.name: Scheduling
components.job: Clinic scheduling / yield management: HOW MUCH TO OVERBOOK each clinic or session, how many extra slots a practice can safely book, WHICH UPCOMING APPOINTMENTS are likely no-shows (tomorrow / next week), who should get a reminder call, access (booking lead time). A past no-show RATE is a literal lookup, not this.
components.why: Translate attendance uncertainty into scheduling choices and reminder priorities.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: No-show prediction and yield management

components.name: Queueing
components.job: Queueing-theory capacity sizing (Erlang C / A / B, square-root staffing): HOW MANY nurses / providers / beds per hour (by hour of week) are needed to keep patient waits under a target (e.g. P(wait > 30 min) <= 10%) or bed blocking under a target (e.g. <= 2%), the chance a patient waits more than N minutes, utilization, sensitivity to +-10% arrivals. Not demand (volume forecasts; staffing only from user-supplied ratios) and not scheduling (overbooking / no-shows).
components.why: Estimate waits, blocking and capacity from arrival/service assumptions rather than guessing from average demand.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Erlang C/A/B and square-root staffing

components.name: Uplift
components.job: Who BENEFITS from outreach or care management (heterogeneous treatment effects): persuadables, uplift / CATE by member, which patients to enrol because the program changes their outcome most, RATE / AUTOC and Qini curves, benefit by decile, targeting within capacity. Not outreach (a worklist ranked by risk / expected value, no causal effect) and not program_effect (did the program work on average, one pooled estimate).
components.why: Distinguish patients likely to benefit from an intervention from patients merely likely to have an adverse outcome.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: CATE, RATE/AUTOC and Qini

components.name: Early Signal
components.job: Early warning: WHICH PATIENTS show the multichannel pattern that usually PRECEDES an admission or ED visit (pre-admission signature, heading toward decompensation), by matched filtering against templates learned from past events. Not one lab trend (trajectory), not time-until curves (survival), not a capacity-limited call list (outreach).
components.why: Look for a temporal pattern preceding events across several signals rather than a single threshold.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Matched filtering over multichannel histories

components.name: Claims Review
components.job: Payment integrity and revenue leakage in DOLLARS: which providers bill unusually vs peers, suspicious billing patterns, where we leak money (denial write-offs, underpayments, take-backs, rework), which claims were underpaid vs comparable claims, denial patterns by payer and reason; review flags ranked by expected dollars. Is-it-out-of-control charts, denial-rate shifts over time and feed health are monitor. A plain dollar total (how much payers paid, net of reversals; total allowed or billed) is literal_lookup.
components.why: Focus review on plausible financial leakage while keeping anomaly flags separate from findings.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Peer comparisons and dollar-ranked payment review

components.name: Knowledge
components.job: EXPLANATION / STRATEGY questions about value-based care itself, not this population's data: how does X work, what is X, explain, how are patients attributed/aligned, compare companies (Aledade vs agilon), CMS/CMMI models and strategy, risk adjustment (HCC V28, RADV), Stars/HEDIS/APP, frameworks (Porter value agenda, Nash population health), evidence on what works (MSSP savings, hotspotting RCT). Cited passages from a curated public-source knowledge base.
components.why: Answer a policy or strategy explanation with relevant source context instead of pretending it came from patient data.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Cited public-source knowledge retrieval

components.name: Risk Adjustment
components.job: CMS-HCC risk adjustment (Medicare Advantage / ACO REACH): RAF and HCCs per patient (V24, V28, payment-year blend), coding gaps, HCC recapture (coded last year, not yet this year), suspect conditions without a diagnosis code (documentation gaps), coding completeness, RAF / risk score by practice, PCP or payer, dollars at stake. An internal (non-HCC) risk score is vbc.
components.why: Apply explicit factor hierarchies and versions instead of inventing a risk formula.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: CMS-HCC V24/V28 and payment-year blends

components.name: Network
components.job: Provider network (patient-sharing graph of clinicians or organisations): which specialists and hospitals our patients actually use, key referral hubs (centrality), provider communities, which PCPs share the most patients, care-team cohesion (care density), referral concentration (HHI), care leaking out of the network by specialty or practice (visits and dollars), steering simulations (if we steer cardiology to practice X, how much leakage do we recover?) and how a practice-pattern change would spread across PCPs (diffusion model). Patient journeys / next steps after an ED visit or discharge are pathway.
components.why: Represent relationships and patient sharing that flat row-by-row summaries miss.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Graph centrality, communities, HHI and diffusion simulations

components.name: Contract Strategy
components.job: Risk-contract STRATEGY: should we move tracks (MSSP BASIC to ENHANCED), which ACO REACH option / risk corridor is best for us, what our upside/downside contract is worth (option value, VaR/CVaR, sensitivities to benchmark and trend), compare two contract offers, what sharing rate / MSR to negotiate (Nash bargaining, break-even against care-management spend), how much downside risk we can take at a confidence level. The settlement amount under ONE stated contract ("what would we earn under X") is vbc.
components.why: Evaluate upside, downside and negotiation assumptions together instead of quoting expected savings alone.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Monte Carlo, option value, VaR/CVaR, sensitivities and Nash bargaining

components.name: Target Trial
components.job: COMPARATIVE EFFECTIVENESS of two drug strategies by target trial emulation (new-user active-comparator design): drug A versus drug B (or high- vs moderate-intensity statins) on a lab change (eGFR decline, A1c, LDL, BP) or time to admission / ED visit / incident condition; explicit protocol, propensity overlap weights or matching, balance, ITT and per-protocol, E-value, negative control. A single drug or program start with no comparator ("did starting X reduce Y") is program_effect; time-to-event curves with no treatment comparison are survival.
components.why: Make treatment-comparison assumptions visible; observed differences alone do not establish causal benefit.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: New-user active-comparator design, propensity balance and sensitivity checks

components.name: Line Of Therapy
components.job: TREATMENT PATTERNS from fills: lines of therapy (first-, second-, third-line regimens), add-on vs switch, treatment sequences (Sankey), switching matrices, time on treatment, persistence / discontinuation and PDC for diabetes, heart-failure GDMT, hypertension, depression, CKD or rheumatoid arthritis. Time to one event after a start with no regimen logic is survival; journeys through care settings are pathway.
components.why: Translate fills into treatment-pattern descriptions without equating dispensing with ingestion.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Regimen episodes, switches, persistence and PDC

components.name: Trial Feasibility
components.job: CLINICAL TRIAL FEASIBILITY: how many patients meet stated inclusion/exclusion criteria (conditions, labs with recency, medications, age, sex), the step-by-step eligibility / attrition funnel, which criteria remove the most patients, eligible patients by site (practice) and investigator (PCP), diversity of the eligible population by race, ethnicity, sex, age and language against stated goals, and expected newly eligible patients (enrolment) per month. A plain count with no trial framing is a literal lookup.
components.why: Show precisely which criterion removes a patient rather than giving an unexplained eligible count.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.
components.status: Registered engine; input, assumption and qualification requirements still apply.
components.example: Eligibility and attrition funnels, site mix and diversity checks

components.name: Loop Closure
components.job: Closing the loop (diagnostic safety): abnormal or critical results with no follow-up or acknowledgement, referrals never completed, report / imaging recommendations not acted on, positive screens without a diagnostic work-up, orders never resulted; open loops with age and owner, close rates by practice or clinician.
components.why: Distinguish an order or referral from a documented completed next step.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.

components.name: Diagnostic Delay
components.job: Missed or delayed diagnoses (SPADE / look-back): how long before a CKD, diabetes, hypertension, heart-failure or colorectal-cancer diagnosis the signals appeared, missed-opportunity visits, patients with diagnostic signals but no diagnosis (review prompts), ED discharges later admitted with a missed diagnosis. HCC coding gaps are risk_adjustment.
components.why: Locate reviewable delays in observed records without presenting a review flag as a confirmed missed diagnosis.
components.economics: Run a specialized implementation when this analysis is requested; model tokens may select the engine, but code calculates it.

components.name: Risk Outcomes
components.job: CMS-style risk-standardized outcome rates (RSRR, observed-to-expected, excess readmission ratio, funnel plot) for readmission, ED revisits, post-discharge ED visits, length of stay or mortality by hospital, practice or PCP. Plain "fair comparison" of PCPs/practices is profile.
components.why: Separate case mix and sample-size effects from raw provider differences.

components.name: Program rules, coverage and attribution
components.job: Apply supplied program requirements and record missing participation, eligibility or attribution evidence.
components.why: A promising patient-level finding does not by itself establish payer coverage or payment entitlement.
components.economics: Reuse explicit program terms and assessments.
components.status: Program-specific contracts; unresolved external facts remain open.

components.name: Persistent plans and work backbone
components.job: Carry the original question, population, evidence, proposed next step and follow-up through durable work items.
components.why: Prevent the answer from losing its premises when handed to an operational workflow.
components.economics: Reuse shared context rather than rereading and reconstructing it at every handoff.
components.status: Implemented synthetic/internal workflow.

components.name: Agents and simulated counterparties
components.job: Exercise enrollment, decline, denial/appeal, appointment, titration and monitoring pathways with simulated counterparties.
components.why: Test how a proposed action handles failures and follow-up, not only the happy-path recommendation.
components.economics: Automation can reduce repeated coordination work; simulation does not establish real-world savings.
components.status: Synthetic workflow capability; no real care execution.

components.name: Population simulator and OAP
components.job: Compare program scenarios, effect assumptions, costs, funnels and outcome-aligned payments.
components.why: Make explicit how a proposed intervention could translate into operational and financial outcomes.
components.economics: Explore alternatives before running a real program.
components.status: Scenario engine; simulated outcomes are not observed effects.

components.name: Evolutionary policy search
components.job: Generate policy candidates, evaluate them in a sandbox and retain candidates according to declared objectives.
components.why: Search targeting/operational choices beyond one hand-written rule while exposing evaluation assumptions.
components.economics: Amortize policy exploration; generated candidates and simulation evaluation have costs.
components.status: Implemented search workflow; not proof of clinical or out-of-sample benefit.

components.name: Value of information and evidence acquisition
components.job: Identify decision-sensitive unknowns, request bounded evidence and reassess when observations arrive.
components.why: Spend effort on the missing fact that can change the decision instead of collecting more irrelevant material.
components.economics: Target review/acquisition effort; keep unknowns explicit.
components.status: Connected bounded acquisition workflow.

components.name: Deliverable composer
components.job: Use Haiku for bounded tool selection and Opus to compose reports and interactive outputs around tool results.
components.why: A polished report must retain the same computed numbers and scope as the analysis.
components.economics: Reuse analytical tools and existing results instead of asking the composer to calculate from prose.
components.status: Configured tool-grounded composition.

components.name: Deliverable verification and writeback
components.job: Check claimed numbers and output contracts before saving an artifact or internal writeback.
components.why: Prevent the final presentation from changing or inventing the analysis.
components.economics: Mechanical validation is reusable across outputs.
components.status: Implemented validation/writeback boundary.

components.name: Application, API, workspaces and hosted packaging
components.job: Expose answers, source context, work and per-question execution/cost through usable interfaces.
components.why: Make the underlying reasoning inspectable by the person who must use the result.
components.economics: One shared service avoids duplicating analysis in separate applications.
components.status: Local product is running; packaging is not external production qualification.

components.name: Compiler design
components.job: Translate supported language into an intermediate representation and executable operators.
components.why: Separate understanding the question from executing it; check scope before computation.
components.economics: Amortize domain reasoning in reusable code.
components.status: Applied throughout planning.

components.name: Type systems and design by contract
components.job: Use typed JSON, parameter schemas and declared input/output shapes.
components.why: Reject a table when a specific count was requested; reject unsupported operation parameters.
components.economics: Cheap checks prevent wasted execution and presentation errors.
components.status: Core engineering mechanism.

components.name: Indexes and query planning
components.job: Use database tables, lexical/dense indexes and ranked schema selection.
components.why: Locate and aggregate the right data without fitting the entire warehouse into a prompt.
components.economics: Database and retrieval work replace unnecessary model context.
components.status: Core retrieval/execution mechanism.

components.name: Memoization and content-addressed caches
components.job: Key reusable vectors, decisions and results by their relevant input/model/code identities.
components.why: Prevent reuse based only on a similar question while its evidence or rules changed.
components.economics: Pay for reusable work once, within its validity boundary.
components.status: Implemented at multiple layers.

components.name: Dependency tracking and invalidation
components.job: Bind results to source/semantic/model identities and rebuild or reject stale work.
components.why: A corrected source record must invalidate the answer that depended on the old version.
components.economics: Recompute affected work rather than indiscriminately rerunning everything.
components.status: Coverage depends on the particular artifact/route.

components.name: Provenance and event history
components.job: Retain source references, offsets, hashes, versions and append-only review history.
components.why: Let an engineer or reviewer reconstruct why a result was produced.
components.economics: Supports reuse and focused correction without repeated manual reconstruction.
components.status: Core traceability mechanism.

components.name: Usage ledger and bounded retries
components.job: Record provider/model, cache reuse, usage estimates, failed attempts and incomplete pricing.
components.why: Unknown API cost must not display as zero; failures and retries count toward economics.
components.economics: Expose actual inference cost and prevent silent repeated paid requests.
components.status: Running; local compute and human effort are separate costs.

components.name: Selective prediction and abstention
components.job: Use task-specific confidence/calibration conditions and visible unsupported/missing-input outcomes.
components.why: A plausible answer is not enough when the requested scope or evidence is unsupported.
components.economics: Escalate selectively rather than calling all models or accepting every cheap result.
components.status: Conditional gates; coverage and error must be assessed together.

components.name: Distillation and verified-work learning
components.job: Turn accepted patterns into query reuse, routing heads, compiler rules or local adapters under separate release checks.
components.why: Retain what was learned without treating model agreement as independent ground truth.
components.economics: Move recurring work from paid inference toward reusable local computation.
components.status: Several implementations; adapter/rule promotion is task-specific.

components.name: Protected evaluation and ablations
components.job: Separate development, calibration and evaluation; compare matched evidence and remove layers to measure their value.
components.why: Architecture complexity cannot demonstrate that a component improves accuracy.
components.economics: Measure cost per correct completed task, including retries and review.
components.status: Harness exists; unvalidated reference sets remain blocked.

components.name: Finite joint observation model
components.job: Model care/channel/documentation hypotheses from observed features.

components.economics: Local probabilistic inference; extra complexity needs measured benefit.
components.status: Research; no automatic clinical fact promotion.

components.name: Tensor-train model
components.job: Factor a high-dimensional interaction model into lower-rank components.

components.economics: Potential compact inference; benefit is not established merely by using tensor methods.
components.status: Research comparator, not default.

components.name: Source distillation and learned outcome models
components.job: Fit or assess narrow readers/predictors using declared source-bound supervision and timing.

components.status: Task-specific research/shadow states; no blanket promotion.
